source.title: Spurious Local Minima are Common in Two-Layer ReLU Neural Networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether gradient descent reaches spurious local minima in a two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem, and measures how often that happens as teacher and student widths vary.
record.gate_note: The paper reports the percentage of 1,000 gradient-descent runs converging near verified spurious local minima for each tested (k,n) pair. Theorems and cited prior-work results are not counted as experimental rows. Table averages for minimal Hessian eigenvalue and objective value are omitted to stay within the row limit; see rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: This is the original source for V2. Its own gradient-descent experiments measure convergence near verified spurious local minima and compare equal-width students with wider students in realizable two-layer ReLU problems.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors prove existence of spurious minima for the listed width pairs and empirically show increasing convergence incidence as equal widths grow. One extra student neuron sharply reduces incidence; none were encountered with at least two extra neurons within the tested range. Non-observation does not prove those wider networks have no spurious minima.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses standard gradient descent from random Xavier initialization on a realizable two-layer ReLU teacher-student population squared-loss problem with Gaussian inputs. It measures spurious-local-minimum convergence, not classification error. The student-width sweep includes equal width and modest over-parameterization.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed incidence changes with teacher and student widths: it rises with equal widths and is lower when the student has one extra neuron; no local minima were found when n ≥ k + 2 in the tested range.
record.problems: The empirical sweep is limited to widths up to 20 and 1,000 runs per (k,n) pair. The reported percentages have no uncertainty estimates. A small fraction of candidate points could not be verified for three stated width pairs; these were 0.1%, 2.4%, and 0.9% of instantiations, respectively. The paper studies population squared loss on Gaussian inputs, not classification benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 1 and 2 also give average minimal Hessian eigenvalues and average objective values for every (k,n) pair. Those 26 condition-specific values for each measure were omitted to preserve space for all reported convergence-rate conditions and two explicit verified-minimum examples. They appear in Section 3, Tables 1 and 2.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and recipe-dependent exceptions.
Training degradation with depth, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization and normalization exceptions.
Initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, recovery, sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: No spurious local minima were encountered for any tested n≥k+2 with n≤20, across 1,000 runs per pair. Record these zero-incidence conditions and their matched equal-width baselines: this directly captures the two-extra-neuron component of V2.
missing.locator: Section 3, experimental sweep and paragraph following Tables 1–2

missing.what: The sweep also includes zero-incidence conditions omitted from the tables: equal widths k=n=1–5 and one-extra-neuron pairs k=1–7 and k=9. Within V2's named width range, (6,7), (7,8), and (9,10) complete the one-extra-neuron comparison.
missing.locator: Section 3, sweep definition and Tables 1–2; Section 2, Remark 1

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels are assigned because this study is an original source for V2. All recorded values match the supplied text. States describe agreement with V2's trend and width benefit, not whether the percentage of failed runs approaches 100%. No part of V2's stated experimental scope is untested once the missing zero-incidence results are included.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, convolutional networks, random or corrupted labels, SGD or Adam, and effects of model size, stopping, and regularization.

The study tests widths up to 20, with standard Xavier random initialization and fixed step size 0.1. It does not test student widths exceeding teacher width by more than 12, other initializations or optimizers, or non-Gaussian input distributions.
Depth, batch normalization, identity shortcuts, plain convolutional networks, Fixup, and CIFAR-10/ImageNet training error.
Activation-matched initializations, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and very deep plain networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss and curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization, training speed, accuracy, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

relation.reason: Its own experiments measure increasing matched-width trapping and the effect of additional student neurons.

tranche.reason: This is V2's original source and establishes the gradient-descent protocol and verified spurious-minimum frequency measure.

source_check.notes: For R26, the matched-width comparison is 93.4% at k=n=19 versus 49.1% at k=19, n=20. No minima encountered with n≥k+2 and n≤20 is empirical non-observation, not proof of elimination. Statement checks cover this study only; other studies, aggregate counts, and independent-replication coverage were not verified. Peer-review status is supplied by pack metadata; code availability is stated in Section 4.1.
